newsitem.title: USA: Intel to build plants in Texas, Costa Rica, China.
newsitem.headline: Intel to build plants in Texas, Costa Rica, China.

text.p: Intel Corp. Wednesday announced plans to build new chip plants in Fort Worth, Texas, Costa Rica and China at a total cost of nearly $1.7 billion.
The nation's largest computer chip maker said it would build an advanced wafer fabrication plant in Fort Worth at a cost of $1.3 billion.
The factory will make advanced chip products and will employ 800 people when at full capacity, it said.

The company said its new plant in San Jose, Costa Rica will employ 2,000 workers over the next few years. The site will initially consist of 400,000-square-feet of manufacturing space and is expected to cost more than $300 million.
At a new conference in San Jose, the country's minister of foreign trade said the Intel plant will operate in a duty-free zone and Intel will not be charged export taxes.
Intel also said that would invest $99 million in a plant in the Waigaoqiao Free Trade Zone of Shanghai to assemble and test flash memory chips.
It will be Intel's first manufacturing plant in China and most of its output will be exported, the company said.

Waigaoqiao, the largest free trade zone in China, offers tax benefits for exporters, Thomas Hartman, an Intel vice president, told reporters in Shanghai. Intel will own 100 percent of the Chinese plant.
